The 20 labels match canonical Mini-IPIP (Donnellan et al. 2006) wording and item order 1-20 exactly. Live table = .sav cell for cell (20 items x 5 levels, all 100 counts identical, 386 ids, 0 missing). ANCHOR REVERSAL (deviation from the source value labels): the .sav gives every IPIP column the same value labels 1=Strongly Disagree..5=Strongly Agree, but the ten *R columns (06R,07R,08R,09R,10R,15R,16R,17R,18R,19R) are stored ALREADY REVERSE-SCORED. Evidence: (a) every R item correlates positively with the forward items of its own facet (+0.18..+0.58; raw reverse-worded items would correlate negatively); (b) stored as-is, facet alphas/means reproduce paper Table 1 (O .65/3.68 vs .65/3.67; C .63/3.50 vs .62/3.50; A .73/4.24 vs .73/4.28; E .71/3.50 vs .71/3.52; N .60/3.37 vs .60/3.38; paper n=375 after 11 outliers dropped vs 386 live), whereas flipping the R items back gives alphas -0.07/-0.28/-0.20/-0.63/-0.33. So for R items option_text is shipped reversed to match the data: resp 1=Strongly Agree ... 5=Strongly Disagree (the answer the respondent actually chose); forward items keep 1=Strongly Disagree..5=Strongly Agree. Neuroticism is keyed high=neurotic (IPIP_09R 'Am relaxed most of the time' and IPIP_19R 'Seldom feel blue' reversed). text_source=translated_substitute: the paper (Procedure) states 'Both the instructions and measures used in the present study were translated into Greek using the front and back translation method'; sample = Democritus University of Thrace students. Checked for Greek wording: .sav variable+value labels (82 variables) have 0 Greek characters; deposit's other files are Supplemental Table B/C PDFs (movie/reading EFA only); the manuscript's Greek-block characters are only statistical symbols (alpha, beta, chi); no questionnaire supplement. English is the study's own .sav labels (translation_source=study_supplied), which are also the canonical English Mini-IPIP. language=Greek. instructions blank: the paper says participants received instructions but does not print them. instrument name is IRW's. Rights: instrument_rights_register.csv row 'International Personality Item Pool (IPIP)' verdict=ship (ipip.ori.org: items 'are in the public domain ... use them for any purpose without asking permission and without paying a fee'); applied, not re-derived. Step 3b: 20 items, 1-5, four per Big Five facet -- matches Mini-IPIP.

Questionnaire constructed by the author for this study (genres drawn from Greek online stores and prior studies); no third-party instrument, so no rights-holder terms apply.

note: PASS with caveats. (1) CODE DERIVATION: the script keeps the .sav column names as item ids (items = columns whose variable label is "Genres of books"), so item IS the source column name; the names are self-describing genre words with the questionnaire position as suffix (Romance_01..Medical_27). The BOOK block is the 27 columns labelled "Genres of books", distinct from the 21 film columns labelled "Genres of movies" (Romance_02, Horror_04, Thriller_18, etc.), and none of the film codes appear in this table. (2) LEVEL-1 CHECK: variable labels for all 27 are the bare block label "Genres of books"; value labels are identical on all 27 (1 Dislike Strongly, 2 Dislike, 3 Neither Like nor Dislike, 4 Like, 5 Like Strongly) and ship verbatim as option_text. The .sav has 0 Greek characters in any variable or value label. (3) WORDING: item_text is the manuscript Appendix "Book genres" list verbatim, whose numbering 1-27 matches the column suffixes 27/27 (e.g. 11 Entertainment/humor = Entertainment_11, 23 Science and nature = Nature_23). Where the appendix and column name differ the appendix wording ships: Comics_12 -> "Comic" (Supplemental Table C prints "Comics"), News_16 -> "News/current events", Nature_23 -> "Science and nature", SciFi_25 -> "Science fiction", Entertainment_11 -> "Entertainment/humor". The manuscript is the accepted author version, not the APA typeset VoR (closed access), so a residual wording difference from the VoR is possible. (4) ADMINISTERED LANGUAGE: Greek ("Both the instructions and measures used in the present study were translated into Greek using the front and back translation method"; genres were drawn from Greek online stores). Greek wording is in neither the deposit (.sav, Supplemental Tables B and C) nor the paper, so per the fallback the study English sits in the base fields, language=Greek, no _translated columns, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. (5) INSTRUCTIONS: the paper only paraphrases the task ("asked to indicate their degree of preference for each genre using a 5-pont scale ranging from 1 (dislike strongly) to 5 (like strongly)"), with no literal instruction text; instructions left blank. The book-genre referent is carried in the instrument field. (6) STEP 3b: live 27 items, resp 1-5, 386 ids, 10378 rows, matches the paper (27 book genres, 1-5 liking scale) and the dictionary description. (7) VERIFICATION: exempt (code IS the source column name). Response-frequency check anyway: live item x level counts equal the .sav counts cell for cell, 135/135 (e.g. Romance_01 45/44/61/131/105, Medical_27 65/70/119/85/45), per-item n 382-386, total 10378. No response-data defects found: no zeros, no out-of-range values, every item uses all 5 levels.
